title: Instrument Dedicated throughput SLI metrics in gateway/runtime (export + aggregation rules)
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Background
Dedicated customers are asking for enforceable throughput guarantees. To do this we need a first-class throughput SLI emitted consistently in the request path, with standardized labels and aggregation rules that match the published measurement standard.

This issue covers:
- emitting raw signals needed for throughput SLIs from the gateway + runtime (prefill/decode) paths
- defining the canonical Prometheus metrics + labels (cardinality-safe)
- documenting how to aggregate into the tier SLI (rate-over-window) used for alerting and customer reporting
- test plan to ensure correctness + stability across deployments

Out of scope
- building the Grafana dashboards + alert rules (tracked in ENG-2201)
- implementing admission control/backpressure behavior (tracked in ENG-2206)

SLI definition alignment
We are targeting the Dedicated primary metric from ADR-0127:
- sustained output tokens/sec computed as rate(output_tokens_total) over a rolling window
- computed per deployment_id and then compared to tier objective (Standard/Performance/Premium)
- excludes planned maintenance windows and customer-induced failures as described in throughput measurement standard

Proposed metrics (names subject to final taxonomy review)
Gateway (authoritative for “accepted requests” + outcomes):
- redwood_gateway_requests_total{deployment_id, customer_id, tier, region, model, route, status}
- redwood_gateway_throttled_total{deployment_id, tier, reason}  (reason: admission_control | quota | overload | internal)
- redwood_gateway_request_inflight{deployment_id, tier}

Runtime/scheduler (authoritative for token counters + queueing):
- redwood_runtime_output_tokens_total{deployment_id, tier, model, region}
- redwood_runtime_input_tokens_total{deployment_id, tier, model, region}
- redwood_runtime_queue_depth{deployment_id, tier}
- redwood_runtime_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{deployment_id, tier}
- redwood_runtime_effective_tokens_per_second{deployment_id, tier} (optional gauge for debugging; SLI should be derived from counters)

Tracing (for debug-only; avoid as dependency for SLI):
- spans for prefill/decode with attributes: deployment_id, tier, model, region, batch_size, sequence_len

Aggregation rules (canonical)
Primary SLI used for SLO:
- throughput_tps = sum by (deployment_id) (rate(redwood_runtime_output_tokens_total{tier!=""}[5m]))
Secondary diagnostic signals:
- throttling_rate = sum(rate(redwood_gateway_throttled_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total[5m]))
- saturation proxies: queue_depth p95, queue_wait p95, inflight

Cardinality constraints
- deployment_id: required; expected <= O(10^3) active deployments
- route: only for gateway request counts; do NOT attach route to runtime token counters
- customer_id: allowed on gateway request counts only if hashed/low-cardinality; default OFF for Dedicated SLI dashboards
- request_id: forbidden

Acceptance criteria
1) Metrics emitted in both gateway and runtime with consistent label keys: deployment_id, tier, region, model (where applicable)
2) A single “source of truth” counter for output tokens that is used by SLO toolkit / Grafana
3) Documentation comment in code + short internal doc snippet describing the SLI query and exclusions
4) Unit tests for label presence + no-regression on metric names
5) Integration/perf test proving the derived SLI matches expected throughput under a fixed workload (within tolerance)
6) Rollout plan: feature-flagged if needed; safe default behavior for older deployments

Test plan
Unit tests
- metric registration tests: ensure counters exist and labels match taxonomy
- label cardinality test: ensure forbidden labels cannot be added in the runtime emitter

Integration tests (staging)
- run fixed benchmark workload (defined by ENG-2216 suite) for 15m with constant concurrency
- compute expected output tokens/sec from workload and compare to rate(output_tokens_total)
- verify no double-counting between gateway and runtime

Canary / production validation
- enable metrics for 1 internal Dedicated deployment
- compare runtime_effective_tokens_per_second gauge vs derived rate(counter)
- verify deployment_id label coverage and stable time series count

Links
- Confluence measurement standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/throughput-measurement-standard.json
- ADR-0127 primary metric: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0127-dedicated-throughput-primary-metric.json
- Metrics taxonomy draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/dedicated-throughput-metrics-taxonomy.json

Notes / open questions
- Do we expose model label for all Dedicated deployments, or only Redwood-managed catalog models? (proposal: always set model to configured model slug; unknown => "custom")
- How do we handle multi-model routing within a Dedicated deployment? (proposal: deployment_id is still stable; model label reflects final selected model; SLI aggregates by deployment_id regardless)
- Window length for SLI (5m vs 10m): SRE preference is 5m for alerting, 30m for customer reporting; confirm in ENG-2201 dashboard spec.
comments: 2025-01-22 (Aisha Bello): Marking P0. We need emission in place before we can finalize SLO burn + dashboard thresholds. Please align names/labels to the taxonomy draft and avoid adding route/request_id anywhere in runtime metrics.

2025-01-24 (Omar El-Sayed): Runtime side: output_tokens_total should increment only on successful decode emission (post-sampler) to match “delivered output tokens”. For streaming, increment as chunks are produced (not at end-of-request) so rate() stays meaningful.

2025-01-25 (Noah Patel): +1 on counter-based SLI. Gauge is okay for debugging but must not be used for SLO. Also watch out for double-counting when speculative decoding is enabled; count only committed tokens.

2025-01-28 (Logan Wright): Implemented emitters behind feature flag dedicated_throughput_metrics_v1. Gateway counters are straightforward; runtime tokens required hooking into the scheduler’s “committed tokens” path. Draft PR up shortly.

2025-02-02 (Sergio Costa): For dashboard queries we’ll likely need tier and region labels present. If model is too high-cardinality for some customers, we can filter it out in panels. Please keep model off any histogram buckets.
2025-02-04 (Logan Wright): PR up (redwood/pr-18422) with standardized labels. Added basic unit tests + migration note. Need one more staging run to validate no series explosion for deployment_id.

2025-02-05 (Rafael Mendes): SRE review: label set looks good. Please update doc comment with the exact SLI query we’ll use (rate over 5m) and note exclusions are applied in reporting layer, not at metric emission time.
